page: Microsoft Azure D4alds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine from the Daldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores with a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes 236 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, but does not feature any GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression/decompression tests scoring in the top 10%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, falls into the average category. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes also register in the average tier. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative bottleneck, performing in the bottom 25%.

This server offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring high single-threaded CPU performance without massive memory footprints. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it less suitable for memory-intensive databases, but highly efficient for compute-bound tasks, text processing, and lightweight web serving. Suitable workloads include single-threaded data processing, software compilation, static web serving, and basic Redis operations.
